correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=2 and 1<=k<n the polytope is full-dimensional in its n²−1 affine hull; the two orthogonal Frobenius projections give exact coordinate and row/column facet support conditions. Optimizing the strictly concave logdet gives the stated phase boundary and semiaxes. An explicit weighted set of all active standardized facet contacts has zero first moment and identity second moment, proving globally unique John optimality via John's theorem; exact rational verifier checked 4,950 (n,k) pairs and 1,510 separate projection identities. The general proof is analytic, not an extrapolation from those finite tests.

General John theory supplies a characterization, not the two-mode closed form. Prior inradius mathematics reaches the same facet-distance transition but does not imply the anisotropic eigenvalue, determinant maximum, or new positive contact orbit. value.rationale: The fixed-cardinality assignment family is a canonical interpolation between simplex and Birkhoff behavior. Its full John ellipsoid is a meaningful natural metric invariant, with a closed two-eigenspace spectrum, exact volume, contact-orbit transition, and strict anisotropy/volume gain in the near-perfect cardinality regime. An inradius alone does not determine these; the result is a global infinite-family classification rather than an arbitrary instance or routine table entry.
